evaluated.name: Profitable Intangible Intensity
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that spend heavily on knowledge and brand building AND still post high operating profitability have an understated asset base, so their measured profitability is a conservative floor on true economic returns and is underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: The product of two industry ranks fires only in the joint corner (high intangible intensity and high profitability), which is exactly the "already-validated" innovator; either theme alone leaves the rank product near the middle. Industry ranking removes sector-level R&D norms so the interaction reflects within-industry differentiation rather than a tech-sector dummy.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Return On Intangible Capital
evaluated.expression: RATIO(MA(oiadp, 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating income per dollar of accumulated intangible capital (five-year R&D stock plus booked purchased intangibles) measures how productively the invisible asset base converts into profit; high values indicate hidden productive capital the market does not capitalize.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a genuine ratio interaction—profitability numerator over an intangible-capital denominator—so it cannot be replicated by either theme alone; scaling by intangible rather than book capital directly targets the mismeasurement channel. Smoothing income over three years suppresses transitory earnings noise, and the denominator is defined only for firms with some intangible base, restricting the signal to the population the story is about.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Hidden Capital ROA Wedge
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ib, SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), RATIO(ib, at)), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: The gap between ROA computed on tangible-only assets and reported ROA equals profitability multiplied by the intangible share of the balance sheet; it measures the dollar magnitude by which conservative accounting understates the earning power per unit of hard capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Algebraically the wedge is ib*intan/(at*(at-intan)), a naturally multiplicative profitability-by-intangible-share term rather than a bolted-on composite, and it is zero for pure tangible firms and negative for intangible-heavy loss makers—precisely the desired asymmetry. Winsorizing controls the explosive tail when intangibles approach total assets.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Profitability Of Intangible Firms
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), 0.7))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-based profitability should be far more informative for intangible-intensive firms, whose accrual earnings are mechanically depressed by expensed R&D and advertising, so the profitability premium is concentrated in the top intangible-intensity tercile.
evaluated.reasoning: The indicator switches the profitability signal on only where the accounting distortion exists, making the effect explicitly conditional rather than additive; operating cash flow bypasses the expensing bias that makes reported earnings understate intangible-rich firms. Firms outside the intangible group receive zero and sit in the middle of the sort, so the long-short spread is driven by the interaction, not by a generic profitability tilt.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Weighted Cash Profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash profitability is most informative where expensed intangible spending distorts accrual earnings, so the profitability premium should scale continuously with intangible intensity rather than switching on at a threshold.
evaluated.reasoning: This directly repairs the gen-0 conditional signal, whose strong FMB slope (3.31) collapsed to zero FF5 alpha because the hard indicator assigned zero to ~70% of firms and produced a degenerate, tie-heavy portfolio sort. Replacing the 0/1 gate with a continuous IND_RANK weight preserves the same interaction (signed profitability amplified by intangible intensity) while restoring a monotone, well-populated cross-sectional spread.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit On Capitalized Intangible Stock
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The relevant measure of hidden capital is the accumulated intangible stock (five-year R&D plus booked purchased intangibles), not the single-year spending flow, so profitable firms with the largest hidden stock relative to reported assets are the most understated.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-0 winner used a one-year flow intensity scaled by sales; this isolates the design choice of stock-versus-flow intangible measurement while holding the rank-product structure and profitability leg fixed. Coalescing missing R&D and intangibles to zero should also widen coverage beyond the 0.143 of the winner, testing whether the effect survives outside the intangible-reporting subsample.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organization Capital Productivity
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: SG&A and advertising build organization and brand capital that is fully expensed; firms that sustain high operating profitability despite heavy organization-capital spending own productive assets that never appear on the balance sheet.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the intangible channel from R&D (science capital) to selling/brand/organizational capital, a distinct and much broader population than R&D reporters, so it tests whether the mechanism is about innovation specifically or about expensed investment generally. Using oibdp (pre-depreciation operating income) keeps the profitability leg from being mechanically depressed by the same expensing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Spend With Rising Profit Path
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible investment is "validated" only when the profitability path is improving; sustained heavy spenders whose operating return on assets is trending upward have demonstrated that the invisible capital is productive.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the level of profitability with its five-year slope, testing whether the market underreacts to the slow accumulation of evidence that intangible outlays are paying off rather than to the static profitability level. It also repairs the gen-0 proposal rejected for lacking a profitability-exclusive variable by using oiadp and xad explicitly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Fully Capitalized Intangible ROA
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(oiadp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Restating the income statement and balance sheet as if intangible outlays were investment yields the firm's true return on total (tangible plus intangible) capital; the market prices reported ROA and therefore misprices firms whose adjusted return is much higher.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike gen-0's Return On Intangible Capital, which divided profit only by intangible capital and mechanically ranked low-intangible firms highest (producing a perverse negative alpha), this scales adjusted profit by the full adjusted capital base so the intangible term enters both numerator and denominator consistently. It tests whether the interaction is better expressed as an accounting restatement than as a rank product.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Unvalidated Intangible Buildup
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, 1), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that rapidly add booked intangible assets (largely acquisition-driven) while their operating profitability deteriorates are capitalizing value that is not being validated by earnings, and should subsequently underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the mirror image of the core story: acquired intangibles overstate rather than understate the productive asset base, so the same profitability-by-intangible interaction should reverse sign when the intangible leg is a purchased-asset increase and the profitability leg is deteriorating. Testing the short side explicitly tells us whether the archive's positive alphas come from the long leg (productive innovators) or the short leg (unvalidated intangible growth).
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Profit On Total Expensed Intangibles
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The full expensed-investment budget (R&D, advertising and SG&A-based organization capital) measures the size of the off-balance-sheet asset base, and firms generating strong operating cash flow despite that spending own validated hidden capital.
evaluated.reasoning: This merges the two best archive mechanisms — the cash-profitability leg from Intangible Weighted Cash Profitability (Sharpe 0.47, alpha 3.7%) and the SG&A intangible leg from Organization Capital Productivity (FMB 4.49) — and tests whether their information is complementary rather than redundant. Cash flow is the right profitability leg because it is immune to the expensing distortion that the intangible leg measures.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Funds From Operations Intangible Weight
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Income before extraordinary items plus depreciation is a cash-earnings proxy available for a much longer history than oancf, so if the intangible-weighted cash-profitability effect is real it should survive with this proxy over a broader sample.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's best Sharpe signal has only 0.091 coverage because statement-of-cash-flows data begins in 1988, which is a genuine robustness risk rather than an edge. Holding the intangible leg identical to Signal 1 isolates the single design choice of cash-flow measurement versus coverage, telling us whether the alpha is a cash-flow effect or a sample-period artifact.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Return On Capitalized Intangible Base
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Restating both the numerator and the capital base as if intangible outlays were investment gives the firm's true cash return on total capital; the market anchors on reported ratios and underprices firms whose restated return is high.
evaluated.reasoning: Fully Capitalized Intangible ROA already delivered a 3.4% alpha with t = 3.06 and the best coverage in the archive, so the restatement structure is worth refining rather than abandoning; this version uses cash flow (which dominated accrual income in the rank-product family) and adds advertising to the capital stock. It keeps the intangible term in both numerator and denominator, avoiding the perverse low-intangible tilt that sank Return On Intangible Capital.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Reliable Profit Intangible Intensity
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Investors discount intangible-intensive firms because their earnings are perceived as fragile and hard to verify; firms whose profitability is not just high but stable relative to its own volatility have demonstrably durable intangible capital and are the most underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces a second-moment channel absent from the archive: the profitability leg is a signal-to-noise ratio (five-year mean divided by five-year volatility) rather than a level or a trend, directly addressing the verification friction that generates the mispricing. The trend-based validation attempt in gen 1 was only marginal (t-alpha 1.79), suggesting reliability rather than direction of change is the missing state variable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organic Minus Acquired Intangible Weight
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Internally generated intangibles are understated by accounting while acquired goodwill is if anything overstated, so cash profitability should be rewarded where intangible capital is organic and penalized where the intangible base is being bought.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-1 short-side test (Unvalidated Intangible Buildup) had the right sign but was weak (t-alpha -1.69), probably because it discarded the profitability level; embedding goodwill growth as a negative weight on cash profitability puts both effects on one continuous scale. It tests whether the archive alpha can be strengthened by separating the direction of the accounting bias rather than treating all intangibles alike.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Brand Capital Margin Power
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xad, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Brand and purchased-intangible capital shows up economically as durable pricing power, so the correct validation of that capital is a persistently high operating margin rather than a high return on reported assets.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive signal scales profits by assets, which mechanically favors asset-light firms and may confound the intangible tilt; margin scaling changes the economic content of the profitability leg to pricing power and provides an independent read on whether the asset-light channel is doing the work. Pairing it with the advertising-plus-booked-intangible leg also isolates the brand channel from the R&D channel that dominates the current archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: FFO Return On Capitalized Intangible Base
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The restated return on total (tangible plus intangible) capital is the core mispricing signal, and it should survive when cash earnings are proxied by income plus depreciation, which is available decades earlier than the cash-flow statement.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash Return On Capitalized Intangible Base is the archive leader (alpha 5.3%, t-alpha 3.68, Sharpe 0.59) but its 0.091 coverage is entirely a post-1988 oancf artifact, so the key open question is whether the result is a sample-period effect. Holding the capitalization structure fixed and swapping only the earnings measure isolates that single design choice and should lift coverage toward 0.15.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Full Intangible Investment Restatement
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If SG&A-based organization capital is a genuine productive asset, then capitalizing it alongside R&D and advertising in both the earnings numerator and the capital base yields the most complete restatement of true return on capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Adding SG&A to the intangible leg raised alpha from 3.7% to 4.4% in the rank-product family, and the restatement family produces the highest alphas overall, so this tests whether the two improvements compound inside the accounting-restatement structure. It also directly tests the limit of the capitalization logic: if treating all SG&A as investment over-inflates the base for retail and service firms, the ratio should degrade relative to Signal 1's narrower base.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Return On Intangible Adjusted Equity
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5))), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: Understated book equity, not understated total assets, is what distorts the valuation anchor investors use; restating shareholders' equity for accumulated intangible investment therefore gives a sharper measure of hidden earning power per dollar of true owners' capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive ratio scales by total assets, which mixes in leverage and working capital; equity scaling changes the economic denominator to the claim investors actually price and makes the hidden-capital adjustment proportionally much larger. Winsorizing controls the tail from small or negative reported equity, which is exactly the population where intangible understatement is most severe.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Committed Intangible Spend Cash Profit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A five-year minimum intangible-spending intensity identifies firms with a committed, non-discretionary innovation and brand budget; profitability earned on top of a persistent commitment reflects durable hidden capital, whereas profitability alongside one-off spending spikes does not.
evaluated.reasoning: The current-year intensity weight cannot distinguish a committed innovator from a firm with a transitory spending burst, and committed spenders are the ones whose intangible stock is genuinely large relative to reported assets. Using the window minimum rather than a moving average makes the persistence requirement strict, testing whether commitment is the state variable that sharpens the conditional weight.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Adjusted Turnover Times Cash Margin
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Validated intangible productivity requires both that the hidden capital base spins fast into revenue and that each revenue dollar converts into cash; firms strong on both dimensions have demonstrably productive intangible assets rather than merely favorable scaling.
evaluated.reasoning: This decomposes the winning restated return into a DuPont pair and requires joint strength via a rank product, which is a different portfolio object than their arithmetic product because it screens out firms achieving a high ratio through one extreme component. It also diagnoses which leg drives the archive leader, informing later consolidation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organic Versus Goodwill Weighted Profit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability signals hidden value when the intangible base is internally built and expensed, but signals overstatement when the intangible base was purchased and booked as goodwill, so the profitability weight should be positive in the first case and negative in the second.
evaluated.reasoning: Brand Capital Margin Power produced a reliable wrong-signed alpha (-2.9%, t -3.04) using booked intangibles, which is informative evidence that capitalized intangibles carry the opposite mispricing to expensed ones; this signal converts that finding into a signed weight instead of discarding it. The rank difference keeps the weight continuous and centered, avoiding the degenerate portfolios that ruined the gen-0 indicator version.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Smoothed Full Intangible Restatement
evaluated.expression: MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)
evaluated.hypothesis: True return on total intangible-inclusive capital is a slow-moving economic state; averaging it over three years removes transitory cash-flow timing noise and should sharpen the statistical reliability of the mispricing signal without changing its economic content.
evaluated.reasoning: Full Intangible Investment Restatement is the archive leader (alpha 7.4%, t-alpha 4.03) but a single-year oancf denominator-free ratio is noisy, and noise in the sorting variable attenuates both the FMB slope and portfolio purity. This isolates the timing choice only, so a higher t-alpha would confirm the mechanism is a persistent state rather than a one-year cash-flow spike.

evaluated.name: Within Industry Intangible Restated Return
evaluated.expression: IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If accounting understatement of intangible capital is mispriced firm by firm, the restated return should predict returns among peers with similar intangible technology, not merely across intangible-heavy versus tangible-heavy industries.
evaluated.reasoning: The raw restatement ratio mechanically favors asset-light industries, so part of the 7.4% alpha could be a static sector tilt that FF5 does not absorb; industry z-scoring strips that tilt and tests the firm-level mispricing claim directly. This is the key robustness diagnostic before consolidating on the restatement family in later generations.

evaluated.name: Self Funded Innovator
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that fund a large intangible investment program entirely out of operating cash flow and still retain surplus cash have proven both the productivity and the financial sustainability of that program, and face no external-financing discount.
evaluated.reasoning: All archive profitability legs measure cash flow gross of intangible spending, which conflates high-margin firms with firms whose investment is barely covered; subtracting the intangible outlay creates a genuine "free cash flow after hidden investment" state that is a different economic object. Weighting it by intangible intensity keeps the interaction focused on firms where the hidden investment program is large enough to matter.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Payoff Inflection
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5))), 5), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The moment intangible investment begins to pay off is when a firm's own restated return on total capital reaches the top of its five-year history; among intangible-intensive firms this inflection is hard for investors to observe because reported earnings remain depressed by expensing.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the cross-sectional level of restated profitability with the firm's position in its own history, a genuinely different information channel that identifies validation events rather than persistently high-quality firms. The gen-1 five-year TREND version was weak (t-alpha 1.79), which suggests a slope estimate is too noisy while a within-firm rank of the restated level is more robust.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Capitalized Intangibles Accrual Trap
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose balance sheets are loaded with purchased intangibles and whose reported earnings exceed operating cash flow are capitalizing and accruing value that has not been validated by cash, and should subsequently underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Booked intangibles have delivered reliably wrong-signed alphas in this archive (Brand Capital Margin Power, t -3.04; Profit On Capitalized Intangible Stock, near zero), which points to an overstatement channel that deserves an explicit short-side test rather than repeated repair attempts. Pairing the booked-intangible leg with accruals rather than a profitability level identifies exactly the firms whose intangible-related earnings lack cash backing.

evaluated.name: Hidden Capital Share Times Restated Return
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Mispricing should be strongest where a high restated return coexists with a large hidden share of true capital, because that is where reported financial statements diverge most from economic reality.
evaluated.reasoning: This unites the two independently successful archive families — the restated-return ratio (alpha 5.3%, t 3.68) and the intangible-intensity conditioning weight (Sharpe 0.47) — but expresses the weight as the intangible fraction of total adjusted capital, which is the exact magnitude of the accounting distortion. If the product beats both parents, the mispricing is genuinely interactive rather than driven by the profitability restatement alone.

evaluated.name: Restated Return Minus Accrual Trap
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3), NEG(MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Expensed intangible capital is understated and purchased intangible capital backed by accruals is overstated, so combining a high restated cash return on total capital with the absence of capitalized-intangible accrual inflation should produce the widest mispricing spread.

evaluated.name: Hidden Share Weighted Restated Return
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)))))

evaluated.name: EBITDA Intangible Restatement Long History
evaluated.expression: RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)))

evaluated.name: Cash Backed Profit Of Intangible Firms
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ib), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)))

Adding it to the coverage-robust composite tests whether commitment is incrementally priced without sacrificing the 0.145 coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Goodwill Only Short Leg Composite
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Only goodwill unambiguously records overpayment for acquired intangibles, whereas identifiable purchased intangibles such as patents and licensed technology may be genuinely productive, so restricting the short leg to goodwill should sharpen the overstatement channel.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has repeatedly bundled goodwill with other capitalized intangibles and never resolved which component drives the reliably negative side, and the standalone goodwill accrual test still produced a -3.9% alpha. Substituting goodwill for total booked intangibles inside the best coverage-robust structure isolates that question while keeping everything else fixed.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Weakest Link Intangible Quality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm qualifies as a validated intangible producer only if it is strong on both dimensions at once — high restated return on total capital and a self-built rather than purchased intangible base — so the binding constraint, not the average, should determine the signal.
evaluated.reasoning: All prior combinations have been additive rank sums or products, which let one extreme channel compensate for a weak one; a minimum imposes a conjunctive requirement that should produce cleaner extreme portfolios and a monotone cross-section. It is a deliberate structural test at full coverage, and if it matches the multi-channel sums it shows the effect is driven by joint qualification rather than aggregation of separate signals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Hidden Share Weighted Long History Return
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Restated profitability should be priced in proportion to how much of the firm's true capital base is unrecognized, and this scaling relationship should hold across the full sample, not only in the cash-flow-statement era.
evaluated.reasoning: The hidden-share weighting structure has generated the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes (FMB 4.99, 4.50, 4.38) but every version used oancf and was confined to 0.077-0.091 coverage, leaving its robustness untested. Rebuilding it on the ebitda restatement gives the highest-slope mechanism a full-sample test and tells us whether the weak alphas of the weighted family were a small-sample artifact.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.name: Profitable Intangible Intensity
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that spend heavily on knowledge and brand building AND still post high operating profitability have an understated asset base, so their measured profitability is a conservative floor on true economic returns and is underpriced.
considered.reasoning: The product of two industry ranks fires only in the joint corner (high intangible intensity and high profitability), which is exactly the "already-validated" innovator; either theme alone leaves the rank product near the middle. Industry ranking removes sector-level R&D norms so the interaction reflects within-industry differentiation rather than a tech-sector dummy.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Return On Intangible Capital
considered.expression: RATIO(MA(oiadp, 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0)))
considered.hypothesis: Operating income per dollar of accumulated intangible capital (five-year R&D stock plus booked purchased intangibles) measures how productively the invisible asset base converts into profit; high values indicate hidden productive capital the market does not capitalize.
considered.reasoning: This is a genuine ratio interaction—profitability numerator over an intangible-capital denominator—so it cannot be replicated by either theme alone; scaling by intangible rather than book capital directly targets the mismeasurement channel. Smoothing income over three years suppresses transitory earnings noise, and the denominator is defined only for firms with some intangible base, restricting the signal to the population the story is about.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Hidden Capital ROA Wedge
considered.expression: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ib, SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), RATIO(ib, at)), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The gap between ROA computed on tangible-only assets and reported ROA equals profitability multiplied by the intangible share of the balance sheet; it measures the dollar magnitude by which conservative accounting understates the earning power per unit of hard capital.
considered.reasoning: Algebraically the wedge is ib*intan/(at*(at-intan)), a naturally multiplicative profitability-by-intangible-share term rather than a bolted-on composite, and it is zero for pure tangible firms and negative for intangible-heavy loss makers—precisely the desired asymmetry. Winsorizing controls the explosive tail when intangibles approach total assets.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Validated R&D Margin Trend
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Sustained R&D investment is only informative when it is being validated by an improving gross profitability path; heavy spenders with rising gross profit-to-assets are building real intangible capital, while heavy spenders with flat or falling margins are burning cash.
considered.reasoning: The interaction is state (R&D intensity level) times slope (five-year gross margin trend), so it identifies innovation that is demonstrably converting into unit economics rather than innovation intensity per se. Investors extrapolate current earnings and underweight the slow-moving trend evidence that intangible spending has begun to pay off.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Profitability Of Intangible Firms
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), 0.7))
considered.hypothesis: Cash-based profitability should be far more informative for intangible-intensive firms, whose accrual earnings are mechanically depressed by expensed R&D and advertising, so the profitability premium is concentrated in the top intangible-intensity tercile.
considered.reasoning: The indicator switches the profitability signal on only where the accounting distortion exists, making the effect explicitly conditional rather than additive; operating cash flow bypasses the expensing bias that makes reported earnings understate intangible-rich firms. Firms outside the intangible group receive zero and sit in the middle of the sort, so the long-short spread is driven by the interaction, not by a generic profitability tilt.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Organic Intangibles Profit Gearing
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Identifiable non-goodwill intangibles (patents, technology, customer lists) represent verifiable productive assets, and when a firm with a large stock of them also earns high gross profitability, the intangibles are demonstrably productive and undervalued; goodwill, by contrast, mostly reflects overpayment and is stripped out.
considered.reasoning: Separating identifiable intangibles from goodwill isolates asset quality within the recorded intangible base, a distinction that neither a pure profitability nor a pure R&D signal can make. The rank product rewards only firms where booked intangible assets are matched by realized gross profit, filtering out acquisitive balance-sheet inflation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Weighted Cash Profitability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Cash profitability is most informative where expensed intangible spending distorts accrual earnings, so the profitability premium should scale continuously with intangible intensity rather than switching on at a threshold.
considered.reasoning: This directly repairs the gen-0 conditional signal, whose strong FMB slope (3.31) collapsed to zero FF5 alpha because the hard indicator assigned zero to ~70% of firms and produced a degenerate, tie-heavy portfolio sort. Replacing the 0/1 gate with a continuous IND_RANK weight preserves the same interaction (signed profitability amplified by intangible intensity) while restoring a monotone, well-populated cross-sectional spread.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit On Capitalized Intangible Stock
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The relevant measure of hidden capital is the accumulated intangible stock (five-year R&D plus booked purchased intangibles), not the single-year spending flow, so profitable firms with the largest hidden stock relative to reported assets are the most understated.
considered.reasoning: The gen-0 winner used a one-year flow intensity scaled by sales; this isolates the design choice of stock-versus-flow intangible measurement while holding the rank-product structure and profitability leg fixed. Coalescing missing R&D and intangibles to zero should also widen coverage beyond the 0.143 of the winner, testing whether the effect survives outside the intangible-reporting subsample.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Organization Capital Productivity
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: SG&A and advertising build organization and brand capital that is fully expensed; firms that sustain high operating profitability despite heavy organization-capital spending own productive assets that never appear on the balance sheet.
considered.reasoning: This changes the intangible channel from R&D (science capital) to selling/brand/organizational capital, a distinct and much broader population than R&D reporters, so it tests whether the mechanism is about innovation specifically or about expensed investment generally. Using oibdp (pre-depreciation operating income) keeps the profitability leg from being mechanically depressed by the same expensing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Spend With Rising Profit Path
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Intangible investment is "validated" only when the profitability path is improving; sustained heavy spenders whose operating return on assets is trending upward have demonstrated that the invisible capital is productive.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the level of profitability with its five-year slope, testing whether the market underreacts to the slow accumulation of evidence that intangible outlays are paying off rather than to the static profitability level. It also repairs the gen-0 proposal rejected for lacking a profitability-exclusive variable by using oiadp and xad explicitly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Fully Capitalized Intangible ROA
considered.expression: RATIO(ADD(oiadp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Restating the income statement and balance sheet as if intangible outlays were investment yields the firm's true return on total (tangible plus intangible) capital; the market prices reported ROA and therefore misprices firms whose adjusted return is much higher.
considered.reasoning: Unlike gen-0's Return On Intangible Capital, which divided profit only by intangible capital and mechanically ranked low-intangible firms highest (producing a perverse negative alpha), this scales adjusted profit by the full adjusted capital base so the intangible term enters both numerator and denominator consistently. It tests whether the interaction is better expressed as an accounting restatement than as a rank product.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Unvalidated Intangible Buildup
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, 1), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that rapidly add booked intangible assets (largely acquisition-driven) while their operating profitability deteriorates are capitalizing value that is not being validated by earnings, and should subsequently underperform.
considered.reasoning: This is the mirror image of the core story: acquired intangibles overstate rather than understate the productive asset base, so the same profitability-by-intangible interaction should reverse sign when the intangible leg is a purchased-asset increase and the profitability leg is deteriorating. Testing the short side explicitly tells us whether the archive's positive alphas come from the long leg (productive innovators) or the short leg (unvalidated intangible growth).
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Profit On Total Expensed Intangibles
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The full expensed-investment budget (R&D, advertising and SG&A-based organization capital) measures the size of the off-balance-sheet asset base, and firms generating strong operating cash flow despite that spending own validated hidden capital.
considered.reasoning: This merges the two best archive mechanisms — the cash-profitability leg from Intangible Weighted Cash Profitability (Sharpe 0.47, alpha 3.7%) and the SG&A intangible leg from Organization Capital Productivity (FMB 4.49) — and tests whether their information is complementary rather than redundant. Cash flow is the right profitability leg because it is immune to the expensing distortion that the intangible leg measures.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funds From Operations Intangible Weight
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Income before extraordinary items plus depreciation is a cash-earnings proxy available for a much longer history than oancf, so if the intangible-weighted cash-profitability effect is real it should survive with this proxy over a broader sample.
considered.reasoning: The archive's best Sharpe signal has only 0.091 coverage because statement-of-cash-flows data begins in 1988, which is a genuine robustness risk rather than an edge. Holding the intangible leg identical to Signal 1 isolates the single design choice of cash-flow measurement versus coverage, telling us whether the alpha is a cash-flow effect or a sample-period artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Return On Capitalized Intangible Base
considered.expression: RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Restating both the numerator and the capital base as if intangible outlays were investment gives the firm's true cash return on total capital; the market anchors on reported ratios and underprices firms whose restated return is high.
considered.reasoning: Fully Capitalized Intangible ROA already delivered a 3.4% alpha with t = 3.06 and the best coverage in the archive, so the restatement structure is worth refining rather than abandoning; this version uses cash flow (which dominated accrual income in the rank-product family) and adds advertising to the capital stock. It keeps the intangible term in both numerator and denominator, avoiding the perverse low-intangible tilt that sank Return On Intangible Capital.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Reliable Profit Intangible Intensity
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Investors discount intangible-intensive firms because their earnings are perceived as fragile and hard to verify; firms whose profitability is not just high but stable relative to its own volatility have demonstrably durable intangible capital and are the most underpriced.
considered.reasoning: This introduces a second-moment channel absent from the archive: the profitability leg is a signal-to-noise ratio (five-year mean divided by five-year volatility) rather than a level or a trend, directly addressing the verification friction that generates the mispricing. The trend-based validation attempt in gen 1 was only marginal (t-alpha 1.79), suggesting reliability rather than direction of change is the missing state variable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Organic Minus Acquired Intangible Weight
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Internally generated intangibles are understated by accounting while acquired goodwill is if anything overstated, so cash profitability should be rewarded where intangible capital is organic and penalized where the intangible base is being bought.
considered.reasoning: The gen-1 short-side test (Unvalidated Intangible Buildup) had the right sign but was weak (t-alpha -1.69), probably because it discarded the profitability level; embedding goodwill growth as a negative weight on cash profitability puts both effects on one continuous scale. It tests whether the archive alpha can be strengthened by separating the direction of the accounting bias rather than treating all intangibles alike.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Brand Capital Margin Power
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xad, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Brand and purchased-intangible capital shows up economically as durable pricing power, so the correct validation of that capital is a persistently high operating margin rather than a high return on reported assets.
considered.reasoning: Every archive signal scales profits by assets, which mechanically favors asset-light firms and may confound the intangible tilt; margin scaling changes the economic content of the profitability leg to pricing power and provides an independent read on whether the asset-light channel is doing the work. Pairing it with the advertising-plus-booked-intangible leg also isolates the brand channel from the R&D channel that dominates the current archive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FFO Return On Capitalized Intangible Base
considered.expression: RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The restated return on total (tangible plus intangible) capital is the core mispricing signal, and it should survive when cash earnings are proxied by income plus depreciation, which is available decades earlier than the cash-flow statement.
considered.reasoning: Cash Return On Capitalized Intangible Base is the archive leader (alpha 5.3%, t-alpha 3.68, Sharpe 0.59) but its 0.091 coverage is entirely a post-1988 oancf artifact, so the key open question is whether the result is a sample-period effect. Holding the capitalization structure fixed and swapping only the earnings measure isolates that single design choice and should lift coverage toward 0.15.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Full Intangible Investment Restatement
considered.expression: RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: If SG&A-based organization capital is a genuine productive asset, then capitalizing it alongside R&D and advertising in both the earnings numerator and the capital base yields the most complete restatement of true return on capital.
considered.reasoning: Adding SG&A to the intangible leg raised alpha from 3.7% to 4.4% in the rank-product family, and the restatement family produces the highest alphas overall, so this tests whether the two improvements compound inside the accounting-restatement structure. It also directly tests the limit of the capitalization logic: if treating all SG&A as investment over-inflates the base for retail and service firms, the ratio should degrade relative to Signal 1's narrower base.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Return On Intangible Adjusted Equity
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5))), 1)
considered.hypothesis: Understated book equity, not understated total assets, is what distorts the valuation anchor investors use; restating shareholders' equity for accumulated intangible investment therefore gives a sharper measure of hidden earning power per dollar of true owners' capital.
considered.reasoning: Every archive ratio scales by total assets, which mixes in leverage and working capital; equity scaling changes the economic denominator to the claim investors actually price and makes the hidden-capital adjustment proportionally much larger. Winsorizing controls the tail from small or negative reported equity, which is exactly the population where intangible understatement is most severe.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Committed Intangible Spend Cash Profit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A five-year minimum intangible-spending intensity identifies firms with a committed, non-discretionary innovation and brand budget; profitability earned on top of a persistent commitment reflects durable hidden capital, whereas profitability alongside one-off spending spikes does not.
considered.reasoning: The current-year intensity weight cannot distinguish a committed innovator from a firm with a transitory spending burst, and committed spenders are the ones whose intangible stock is genuinely large relative to reported assets. Using the window minimum rather than a moving average makes the persistence requirement strict, testing whether commitment is the state variable that sharpens the conditional weight.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Adjusted Turnover Times Cash Margin
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, sale)))
considered.hypothesis: Validated intangible productivity requires both that the hidden capital base spins fast into revenue and that each revenue dollar converts into cash; firms strong on both dimensions have demonstrably productive intangible assets rather than merely favorable scaling.
considered.reasoning: This decomposes the winning restated return into a DuPont pair and requires joint strength via a rank product, which is a different portfolio object than their arithmetic product because it screens out firms achieving a high ratio through one extreme component. It also diagnoses which leg drives the archive leader, informing later consolidation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Organic Versus Goodwill Weighted Profit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability signals hidden value when the intangible base is internally built and expensed, but signals overstatement when the intangible base was purchased and booked as goodwill, so the profitability weight should be positive in the first case and negative in the second.
considered.reasoning: Brand Capital Margin Power produced a reliable wrong-signed alpha (-2.9%, t -3.04) using booked intangibles, which is informative evidence that capitalized intangibles carry the opposite mispricing to expensed ones; this signal converts that finding into a signed weight instead of discarding it. The rank difference keeps the weight continuous and centered, avoiding the degenerate portfolios that ruined the gen-0 indicator version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Smoothed Full Intangible Restatement
considered.expression: MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)
considered.hypothesis: True return on total intangible-inclusive capital is a slow-moving economic state; averaging it over three years removes transitory cash-flow timing noise and should sharpen the statistical reliability of the mispricing signal without changing its economic content.
considered.reasoning: Full Intangible Investment Restatement is the archive leader (alpha 7.4%, t-alpha 4.03) but a single-year oancf denominator-free ratio is noisy, and noise in the sorting variable attenuates both the FMB slope and portfolio purity. This isolates the timing choice only, so a higher t-alpha would confirm the mechanism is a persistent state rather than a one-year cash-flow spike.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Within Industry Intangible Restated Return
considered.expression: IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(xsga, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: If accounting understatement of intangible capital is mispriced firm by firm, the restated return should predict returns among peers with similar intangible technology, not merely across intangible-heavy versus tangible-heavy industries.
considered.reasoning: The raw restatement ratio mechanically favors asset-light industries, so part of the 7.4% alpha could be a static sector tilt that FF5 does not absorb; industry z-scoring strips that tilt and tests the firm-level mispricing claim directly. This is the key robustness diagnostic before consolidating on the restatement family in later generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Funded Innovator
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that fund a large intangible investment program entirely out of operating cash flow and still retain surplus cash have proven both the productivity and the financial sustainability of that program, and face no external-financing discount.
considered.reasoning: All archive profitability legs measure cash flow gross of intangible spending, which conflates high-margin firms with firms whose investment is barely covered; subtracting the intangible outlay creates a genuine "free cash flow after hidden investment" state that is a different economic object. Weighting it by intangible intensity keeps the interaction focused on firms where the hidden investment program is large enough to matter.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Payoff Inflection
considered.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5))), 5), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The moment intangible investment begins to pay off is when a firm's own restated return on total capital reaches the top of its five-year history; among intangible-intensive firms this inflection is hard for investors to observe because reported earnings remain depressed by expensing.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the cross-sectional level of restated profitability with the firm's position in its own history, a genuinely different information channel that identifies validation events rather than persistently high-quality firms. The gen-1 five-year TREND version was weak (t-alpha 1.79), which suggests a slope estimate is too noisy while a within-firm rank of the restated level is more robust.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Capitalized Intangibles Accrual Trap
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose balance sheets are loaded with purchased intangibles and whose reported earnings exceed operating cash flow are capitalizing and accruing value that has not been validated by cash, and should subsequently underperform.
considered.reasoning: Booked intangibles have delivered reliably wrong-signed alphas in this archive (Brand Capital Margin Power, t -3.04; Profit On Capitalized Intangible Stock, near zero), which points to an overstatement channel that deserves an explicit short-side test rather than repeated repair attempts. considered.name: Hidden Capital Share Times Restated Return

considered.name: EBITDA Intangible Restatement Long History
considered.expression: RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)))

considered.hypothesis: Validated intangible productivity is a within-industry phenomenon: relative to peers using the same technology, firms with higher restated returns, larger unrecognized capital shares and smaller purchased intangible bases are underpriced.
considered.reasoning: The long-history three-channel composite is the archive's best all-around signal (FMB 3.69, alpha 5.9%, t-alpha 4.80 at 0.145 coverage), and industry neutralization previously improved the restatement's cross-sectional slope (3.72 to 4.02) by stripping the asset-light sector tilt. Applying it to all three channels before ranking should raise both the slope and the Sharpe, whose 0.417 is the composite's weakest diagnostic.

considered.name: Cash Preferred Intangible Composite

considered.hypothesis: The cash-flow-based restatement is the economically superior measure of intangible productivity, but where cash-flow data are unavailable the earnings-based restatement captures the same economics, so a preference-ordered fallback should dominate either version alone.
considered.reasoning: The two three-channel composites are the archive's best alpha (7.9%, Sharpe 0.59 at 0.078 coverage) and best coverage-robust signal (5.9%, t 4.80 at 0.145 coverage), and both output comparable rank-sum scales, so COALESCE is a measurement-availability fallback rather than a coverage patch. This is the natural final consolidation: it keeps the strongest measurement where it exists and triples the usable sample where it does not.

considered.hypothesis: Only goodwill unambiguously records overpayment for acquired intangibles, whereas identifiable purchased intangibles such as patents and licensed technology may be genuinely productive, so restricting the short leg to goodwill should sharpen the overstatement channel.
considered.reasoning: The archive has repeatedly bundled goodwill with other capitalized intangibles and never resolved which component drives the reliably negative side, and the standalone goodwill accrual test still produced a -3.9% alpha. Substituting goodwill for total booked intangibles inside the best coverage-robust structure isolates that question while keeping everything else fixed.

considered.name: Weakest Link Intangible Quality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xsga, 0), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5))), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm qualifies as a validated intangible producer only if it is strong on both dimensions at once — high restated return on total capital and a self-built rather than purchased intangible base — so the binding constraint, not the average, should determine the signal.
considered.reasoning: All prior combinations have been additive rank sums or products, which let one extreme channel compensate for a weak one; a minimum imposes a conjunctive requirement that should produce cleaner extreme portfolios and a monotone cross-section. It is a deliberate structural test at full coverage, and if it matches the multi-channel sums it shows the effect is driven by joint qualification rather than aggregation of separate signals.

considered.hypothesis: Restated profitability should be priced in proportion to how much of the firm's true capital base is unrecognized, and this scaling relationship should hold across the full sample, not only in the cash-flow-statement era.
considered.reasoning: The hidden-share weighting structure has generated the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes (FMB 4.99, 4.50, 4.38) but every version used oancf and was confined to 0.077-0.091 coverage, leaving its robustness untested. Rebuilding it on the ebitda restatement gives the highest-slope mechanism a full-sample test and tells us whether the weak alphas of the weighted family were a small-sample artifact.
